+#ifndef STREAM_H
+#define STREAM_H
+
+#include "rax.h"
+
+/* Stream item ID: a 128 bit number composed of a milliseconds time and
+ * a sequence counter. IDs generated in the same millisecond (or in a past
+ * millisecond if the clock jumped backward) will use the millisecond time
+ * of the latest generated ID and an incremented sequence. */
+typedef struct streamID {
+    uint64_t ms;        /* Unix time in milliseconds. */
+    uint64_t seq;       /* Sequence number. */
+} streamID;
+
+typedef struct stream {
+    rax *rax;               /* The radix tree holding the stream. */
+    uint64_t length;        /* Number of elements inside this stream. */
+    streamID last_id;       /* Zero if there are yet no items. */
+} stream;
+
+#endif

part.text:
## Answer

**Redis first got the streams data type on 30 August 2017** (author date), with the initial implementation landing in the `unstable` branch. It was authored by Salvatore Sanfilippo (antirez) and shipped publicly in **Redis 5.0**.

### Supporting commit

```
commit 79866a6361829ed0602dedff9cb378c66977227a
Author: antirez <antirez@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 30 12:40:27 2017 +0200

    Streams: 12 commits squashed into the initial Streams implementation.
```

This is the **first** commit in the repository to touch `src/t_stream.c` or `src/stream.h`, and the first to add `xadd` to the command table (verified with `git log --diff-filter=A`, `git log -S'"xadd"' --reverse`, and by confirming no XADD/Streams commits exist before this date).

### Quoted evidence from the diff

It registers `XADD` (and `XRANGE`) in the command table in `src/server.c`:

```diff
     {"pfdebug",pfdebugCommand,-3,"w",0,NULL,0,0,0,0,0},
+    {"xadd",xaddCommand,-4,"wmF",0,NULL,1,1,1,0,0},
+    {"xrange",xrangeCommand,-4,"r",0,NULL,1,1,1,0,0},
```

It creates the new `src/stream.h` defining the core type:

```diff
+/* Stream item ID: a 128 bit number composed of a milliseconds time and
+ * a sequence counter. ... */
+typedef struct streamID {
+    uint64_t ms;        /* Unix time in milliseconds. */
+    uint64_t seq;       /* Sequence number. */
+} streamID;
+
+typedef struct stream {
+    rax *rax;               /* The radix tree holding the stream. */
+    uint64_t length;        /* Number of elements inside this stream. */
+    streamID last_id;       /* Zero if there are yet no items. */
+} stream;
```

And it adds `src/t_stream.c` (376 lines) with the command implementations:

```diff
+/* XADD key [field value] [field value] ... */
+void xaddCommand(client *c) {
...
+/* XRANGE key start end [COUNT <n>] */
+void xrangeCommand(client *c) {
```

The full commit adds 1,323 lines across 12 files, including the brand-new `listpack.c` encoding and `rax.c` radix-tree changes that back the "radix tree of listpacks" stream encoding described in the code comments.

### Notes on dating

- **Author date is 2017-08-30**, but the **commit date is 2017-12-01** — antirez developed streams on a side branch and squashed/rebased 12 commits onto `unstable` in December 2017. Either date is defensible; 2017-08-30 is when the work was originally written.
- Follow-up commits fill out the type over the following days/months: `100d43c1a` (OBJ_STREAM = 6), `485014cc7` (RDB saving), `edd70c199` (RDB loading), `ec9bbe96b` (XLEN), etc.
- This repository checkout has **no tags**, so the 5.0 release association comes from the release timeline rather than in-repo tag evidence.

I did not modify any files.
